items.title: The actual implemented two-layer Picard phase kernel

source.anchor: Algorithm 3.1 steps 1–4, HTML lines 282–306; Appendix D.1 (D.1), Algorithm D.2 and Lemma D.3, lines 2138–2164
source.attribution: Fan Chen, Sinho Chewi, Jianfeng Lu and Matthew S. Zhang. Samplinglib supplies the explicit measurable kernel construction; deterministic quadrature data remain a separate adapter.

items.statement: Attributed implementation component of Algorithm 3.1 with Appendix D.1/D.2 approximate proximal queries, not a convergence theorem. Under the normalized C2 Hessian bounds and 0<eta<=c<1, eps>0, construct one measurable stopped proximal map q, its exact proximal comparison p, and its successful gradient-test count N+1. For h>=0 and supplied finite deterministic node and quadrature arrays, draw independent zeta0,zeta1,G0,G1 from the product of two standard Gaussian laws and two finite products of standard Gaussian laws. Set a=exp(-h/2), sigma=sqrt(1-exp(-h)), P0=a P+sigma zeta0, Y0_i=X+t_i P0, Z0_j=grad V(q(Y0_j)+sqrt(eta)G0_j), Y1_i=Y0_i-sum_j omega_ij Z0_j, Z1_j=grad V(q(Y1_j)+sqrt(eta)G1_j), Xnext=X+h P0-sum_j positionWeight_j Z1_j and Pnext=a(P0-sum_j momentumWeight_j Z1_j)+sigma zeta1. The joint update Phi is measurable and defines a Markov kernel K(s,.)=map(Phi(s,.),gamma); at every queried y the actual finite interpreter with fuel N(y)+1 returns (q(y),N(y)+1) and ||q(y)-p(y)||<=eps. Source node/weight construction and the repeated-run accuracy/cost theorems remain separate.
assumptions: E is a complete finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel sigma-algebra; the index type is finite.
V is C2, kappa >= 1 and kappa^(-1)||v||^2 <= D2V(x)[v,v] <= ||v||^2 for every x,v.
t, omega, positionWeight and momentumWeight are supplied finite real arrays. Their source quadrature definitions and bounds are not conclusions of this interface.

formulae.label: First refresh and layer
formulae.tex: P_0=aP+\sigma\zeta_0,\quad Y_i^0=X+t_iP_0,\quad Z_j^0=\nabla V(q(Y_j^0)+\sqrt\eta G_j^0),\quad Y_i^1=Y_i^0-\sum_j\omega_{ij}Z_j^0.

formulae.label: Second layer and refresh
formulae.tex: Z_j^1=\nabla V(q(Y_j^1)+\sqrt\eta G_j^1),\quad X^+=X+hP_0-\sum_j b_jZ_j^1,\quad P^+=a(P_0-\sum_j m_jZ_j^1)+\sigma\zeta_1.

bindings.boundary: One actual gradient-only two-layer phase with supplied finite deterministic coefficients. The Chebyshev-Lobatto coefficient construction and instantiation, repeated phase law, state/moment bounds, local and accumulated error, expected work, terminal FORS, proxy warmness and both main theorems remain separate.

assumption_deltas.source: The normalized C2 Hessian bounds and Algorithm D.2 parameter range.
assumption_deltas.lean: V is C2, kappa >= 1 and kappa^(-1)||v||^2 <= D2V(x)[v,v] <= ||v||^2 for every x,v. 0 < eta <= c < 1, eps > 0 and h >= 0.
assumption_deltas.reason: The parent supplies the actual finite stopping certificate. h=0 includes a degenerate limiting phase without enlarging the sampling schedule.

assumption_deltas.source: Algorithm 3.1 uses source Chebyshev–Lobatto nodes and integral weights.
assumption_deltas.lean: t, omega, positionWeight and momentumWeight are supplied finite real arrays. Their source quadrature definitions and bounds are not conclusions of this interface.
assumption_deltas.reason: This constructs the finite coefficient-parametric implementation interface. Identifying these arrays with the source definitions is explicitly unproved; no source convergence credit follows.

assumption_deltas.source: Independent standard Gaussian variables in Algorithm 3.1.
assumption_deltas.lean: Two standard Gaussian factors and two finite independent Gaussian-array factors, followed by an explicit joint measurable update.
assumption_deltas.reason: Canonical product probability laws and Borel measurability supply omitted stochastic semantics; no moment or integrability premise is needed just to define a Markov kernel.

assumption_deltas.source: A Euclidean state space with J>=2 nodes and positive phase length.
assumption_deltas.lean: An arbitrary complete finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space, finite index type and nonnegative h.
assumption_deltas.reason: The purely measurable phase construction also includes degenerate dimensions, empty arrays and h=0. Source schedules remain obligations of consumers.
